chosen.premise: Tentacool can wash ashore completely shriveled, yet revive when tossed back into the sea or soaked in water.
chosen.hook: A dried-out Tentacool may not be dead—it may just need water.
chosen.visualIdea: Animate Tentacool shrinking into a dry beach remnant, then swelling back to life underwater.
chosen.note: Strong transformation premise with a memorable survival twist: a shriveled beach Tentacool can still revive in water. Multiple entries support both dehydration and revival, making this ideal for a visual short.

candidates.premise: Tentacool is 99% water, while the remaining 1% contains the organ that makes its poison.
candidates.hook: Tentacool is almost entirely water—but that tiny remainder is toxic.
candidates.visualIdea: Show Tentacool filling a 99% water gauge, then zoom into the tiny 1% poison section.
candidates.note: An unusually precise biological-sounding contradiction: an almost entirely watery body contains the poison-making organ. The 99%/1% split is highly visual and directly supported by the Ultra Moon entry.

candidates.premise: Tentacool absorbs sunlight, refracts it through water inside its body, and fires beams from its crystal-like eyes.
candidates.hook: Tentacool turns sunlight and body water into beam attacks.
candidates.visualIdea: Trace sunlight into Tentacool's watery body, then route the energy toward its crystal-like eyes.
candidates.note: Distinctive internal mechanism with excellent animation potential. Slightly less surprising because beam-shooting is familiar in Pokémon, but the sunlight-refraction-through-water explanation is specific and well supported.

candidates.premise: Tentacool's poisonous tentacles can break off, but the Pokémon eventually grows them back.
candidates.hook: Tentacool can lose its poisonous tentacles—and regrow them.
candidates.visualIdea: Show a poisonous tentacle snapping off, followed by a fast regrowth time-lapse.
candidates.note: Excellent concise fact and very visual body-horror transformation. It relies on a single Pokédex entry, so the premise is well supported but less corroborated than the top choices.

candidates.premise: Tentacool blends into the sea so well that swimmers may not notice it until its toxic tentacles sting.
candidates.hook: You might not see Tentacool until it has already stung you.
candidates.visualIdea: Fade Tentacool into ocean footage, reveal only a sudden tentacle strike and warning sting flash.
candidates.note: The concealment-to-sting progression is clear and well supported, but the general idea resembles real jellyfish behavior and other ambush Pokémon. Strong visual hook, somewhat less uniquely Tentacool.

candidates.premise: At level 30, Tentacool evolves into Tentacruel while keeping its Water and Poison typing.
candidates.hook: At level 30, Tentacool evolves without changing either of its types.
candidates.visualIdea: Place Tentacool and Tentacruel side by side as a level counter hits 30, with both types unchanged.
candidates.note: Accurate and easy to show, but evolution level and retained typing are routine Pokémon facts. It does not reveal much that is uniquely surprising about Tentacool.

rounds.request: No stronger angle is required; the episode should center on Tentacool surviving dehydration and reviving when returned to water. A stronger alternative would need an equally specific, well-supported contradiction with a clear transformation viewers can watch.
